uncited: CoR-GS operates by enforcing consistency between two distinct Gaussian field representations derived from the same sparse input views.
The core mechanism involves generating two independent reconstructions and evaluating their agreement to identify and remove unreliable Gaussians.
- Sparse set of input views (images and camera poses).
- Initial set of 3D Gaussians (typically from a standard 3DGS initialization).
- Refined set of 3D Gaussians with improved geometric and photometric consistency.
- Two independent sets of Gaussian parameters (position, covariance, opacity, SH coefficients) are maintained during the comparison phase.
- A mask or filter is applied to the union of Gaussians to discard those failing the consistency check.
**Dual Reconstruction:** Train two independent Gaussian fields from the same sparse input views.
**Comparison:** Render views from both reconstructions and compare the results.
**Refinement:** The remaining Gaussians form the final, consistent representation.
- Inaccurate Gaussians: The method relies on the ability to distinguish accurate from inaccurate Gaussians via the consistency check.
If both reconstructions are equally poor, the method may not improve results.
